# Edge-Care pilot partnership brief

## The opportunity

Explore a private, multilingual community health kiosk that helps people describe symptoms, check a useful history, and reach a clinician-reviewed next step. Focus on people facing distance, language, uncertainty or discomfort when seeking care.

## Current status

Independent project with a working synthetic prototype across kiosk intake, patient referral wallet, clinician verification and a web workspace. Demo appointments do not connect to real clinics. Clinical safety, language accuracy, authentication and outcomes require further validation.

## Proposed pilot

- Two community sites: one urban and one rural.
- 160 main-study adults, with additional co-design and soft-launch participants.
- Eight weeks of main recruitment, approximately 22 weeks overall, subject to readiness and required reviews.
- Comparison of kiosk intake with an existing supported route into care.
- Clinician-reviewed guidance and separately evaluated AI urgency recommendations.
- Outcomes: completed appropriate assessments, safety, understanding, language performance and pathway costs.
- Illustrative budget: €101,000, excluding major new development, regulatory fees, separately required insurance and downstream care costs.

## Partnership discussion

We propose discussing clinical and community partners, referral capacity, language validation, evaluation design, governance, funding and implementation expertise. This proposal aligns with published health-equity and collaborative innovation priorities; it is not an existing partnership or endorsement by AstraZeneca.
